$comment: 50 voices for Nicholas AC Mumford — Friday 2026-11-28. Performed by RSP (and LINA by his wife) in NOIZYSTDZ. Each voice: category, preset (live FX heard in cans while performing — recordings stay clean), a 20–40 s script, target length. `sleep` voices are LINA-first.

voices.name: Captain Brassbuckle
voices.script: Hoist the colours, you barnacle-brained beauties! Captain Brassbuckle doesn't chase treasure — treasure chases HIM!

voices.name: Pip the Bottle Sprite
voices.script: Ooh ooh ooh — you opened the cork! Three wishes? No no no. Three SNACKS. That's the deal, that's always been the deal.

voices.name: Grandpa Thunder
voices.script: When I was young the sky was smaller. Come, little one — sit on this cloud. I'll tell you how the rain learned to sing.

voices.name: Dr. Ferdinand Fizz
voices.script: Zis is not an explosion! Zis is a RESULT! Write it down, Igor — 'subject glows, but politely'.

voices.name: Marcus the Mall Cop
voices.script: Sir. Sir. The pretzel kiosk is a NO-RUN zone. I don't make the rules. Okay, I made that one.

voices.name: Zorbax, Conqueror of Zone 4
voices.script: Tremble, Earth-things! I, Zorbax, demand your— wait, is that a dog? Can I pet the dog? Conquest can wait.

voices.name: Benny the Bus
voices.script: All aboard! Next stop: ANYWHERE! Hold on tight, friends — Benny's got brand new tires and a song in his engine!

voices.name: Sir Reginald Fluffington III
voices.script: One does not simply 'come here, kitty'. One is summoned. With tuna. On the good plate.

voices.name: Coach Rocco
voices.script: Listen up! I don't care if the other team's got robots. We got HEART. And a kid named Dale who can kick a ball into orbit.

voices.name: The Narrator Who Lies
voices.script: Our hero entered the cave bravely. He did not scream. There is no footage of the screaming. Moving on.

voices.name: Gloop
voices.script: Gloop… hungry. Gloop… lonely. Gloop… would like… friend. Or sandwich. Friend who is sandwich — best.

voices.name: Detective Mabel Quill
voices.script: The bread was gone. The pond was quiet. Too quiet. Somebody in this park knew something, and I was gonna find out who.

voices.name: Prince Dorian the Dramatic
voices.script: Banished?! From the DESSERT TABLE?! Mother, this is the cruellest day in the history of days!

voices.name: Unit 7-B
voices.script: Query: the sensation in my chassis when the small human laughed. Diagnostic found no fault. Recommend… more laughing.

voices.name: Auntie Flambé
voices.script: We do NOT measure, darling. We FEEL the garlic. Close your eyes. Is it enough? It is NEVER enough.

voices.name: Old Man Winter
voices.script: Shhh. Hear that? That's the sound of every pond in the valley going still. I did that. You're welcome.

voices.name: Tuck the Turtle
voices.script: Dude. The race isn't about being fast. It's about… wait, what was I saying? Right. Lettuce.

voices.name: Madame Zelda's Parrot
voices.script: BRAWK! I see… I see… a tall dark stranger! BRAWK! It's the mailman. It's always the mailman.

voices.name: Sergeant Pebble
voices.script: You call that ROLLING, maggot?! My grandmother rolled downhill with more conviction, and she was GRAVEL!

voices.name: The Moon
voices.script: Every night the same question: 'Are you full or new?' I'm just the Moon, pal. I'm doing my best up here.

voices.name: The Documentary
voices.script: Here, in the last light of autumn, the monarch begins a journey no single butterfly will finish. Four generations. Three thousand miles. One instinct.

voices.name: The Trailer
voices.script: In a world that forgot how to listen… one voice remembered. This Friday. Everything changes.

voices.name: The Audiobook — Literary
voices.script: I was eleven the summer my father stopped speaking. Not angry — just quiet, the way a house goes quiet after the last guest leaves.

voices.name: The Audiobook — Thriller
voices.script: The phone rang twice and stopped. That was the signal. Kessler had ninety seconds before the second car arrived.

voices.name: The Luxury Brand
voices.script: Crafted by hand. Measured in generations. Some things aren't bought. They're inherited.

voices.name: The Tech Keynote
voices.script: We asked a simple question: what if your voice was yours? Not licensed. Not scraped. Yours. That's NOIZYVOX.

voices.name: The Museum Audio Guide
voices.script: Stop twelve. Notice the brushwork along the left edge — the artist painted this in a single night, by candlelight, in 1889.

voices.name: The Sports Hype
voices.script: Fourth quarter. Down by three. Eleven seconds. This is why you play. This is why you WATCH.

voices.name: The Public Service
voices.script: A working smoke alarm doubles your chance of getting out. Test yours tonight. It takes ten seconds.

voices.name: The History Channel
voices.script: By dawn on the sixth of June, the fate of a continent rested on a strip of sand five miles long.

voices.name: The Kids' Educational
voices.script: Did you know an octopus has three hearts? THREE! And when it swims, one of them actually stops. Let's find out why!

voices.name: The Ottawa Tourism
voices.script: Skate the world's largest rink. Stand where a country was argued into being. Ottawa — closer than you think.

voices.name: The Corporate Explainer
voices.script: Here's how it works. You record once. We never resell it. Every use is tracked, every payment lands in your wallet in under a second.

voices.name: The Poem
voices.script: Do not go gentle — no. Not that one. Something smaller: the kettle, the window, the way the dog waits at the door.

voices.name: The Voice of GOD (MC96)
voices.script: Good evening, Robert. All twelve Workers are green. LUCY is charging. LINA's first session is in the morning. Sleep well.

voices.name: The Lighthouse Keeper
voices.script: The lamp turns once every twelve seconds. You can count them if you like… or just let them pass. One… the water settles… two… the gulls are home…

voices.name: Rain on the Cabin Roof
voices.script: There's nowhere you need to be. The fire has done its work. The rain is doing its work. Your only job now is to be warm.

voices.name: The Night Train
voices.script: The train hums. Fields pass in the dark you'll never see. Somewhere a town turns off its last light… and you don't have to watch it.

voices.name: Body Scan
voices.script: Notice your feet. Not to change them. Just to notice. Now your knees… heavy. Your hands… let them be exactly where they are.

voices.name: Counting Down from Fifty
voices.script: Fifty… the room is dim… forty-nine… your breath is slower than you think… forty-eight… there's no need to reach forty.

voices.name: The Garden After Dark
voices.script: The jasmine opens at night. You can't see it. But the air changes… sweeter… and the moths know before you do.

voices.name: Snowfall
voices.script: Each flake takes its time. There is no hurry in snow. The street disappears… the cars… the footprints… even the sound.

voices.name: The Old Library
voices.script: Somewhere in the stacks a clock ticks you can't quite locate. You've read this page three times. That's fine. The book will wait.

voices.name: Floating
voices.script: The water holds you. You don't have to hold anything back. Your ears below the surface… the world turns to a hum…

voices.name: Bedtime Story — The Fox Who Collected Mornings
voices.script: Once there was a fox who kept every sunrise in a jar. Not the light — the feeling. On hard nights she'd open one… and the whole den would warm.

voices.name: The Desert at Night
voices.script: The sand lets go of the day's heat. The sky is more stars than dark. You are very small, and that is a relief.

voices.name: Grandfather's Porch
voices.script: The boards creak in rhythm. Crickets. A screen door somewhere down the road. Nobody's asking you anything tonight.

voices.name: Breath Pacing
voices.script: In… two… three… four. Hold… let it be easy… Out… slow… all the way… and again. There's nothing on the other side of this breath but the next one.

voices.name: The Ferry at Dusk
voices.script: The engine is a heartbeat under the deck. The far shore has lights now. You'll get there. You always get there. No need to watch.

voices.name: LINA — Goodnight
voices.note: LINA introduces herself, closes the reel
voices.script: I'm LINA. I was made from one real voice, given freely, kept safe. I'm here when the house is quiet. Goodnight, Nicholas. Goodnight, Robert.
